thread:
deploy-bot: Starting blue/green rollout for release/2026.03.15 -> apac regions. Canary traffic 15% to blue in ap-northeast and ap-southeast (split=15%). Adjusting geo-weighting across regions. (job id dply/1796004321)
Jordan: getting pager - multiple 502/504s from APAC customers, looks tied to ap-northeast. Paging SRE. :rotating_light:
Mike: Yep alerts: api.gateway.latency and api.gateway.5xx in ap-northeast. Can someone take triage?
SRE-Oncall: I'm on. Looking at traces - upstream read timeouts and connection resets to model-proxy pool in ap-northeast.
Kei: I can repro a 504 from ap-northeast on /v1/chat. curl shows body: 
```
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
{"error":"upstream unreachable"}
```
Ops-Bot: Noted deploy job started ~1796004280. Blue image pushed to ap-northeast ~20s after ap-southeast.
Jordan: Any chance traffic is unevenly split? We intended same weights but maybe DNS geo-weighting mismatch.
Ops: Running dig from ap-northeast edge now.
Ops: ap-northeast resolv results:
```
> dig +short api.service.internal A
192.168.10.7  # blue primary
192.168.10.21 # green
```
Ops: ap-southeast resolv results:
```
> dig +short api.service.internal A
192.168.10.21 # green
192.168.10.7  # blue
```
SRE-Oncall: That suggests ap-northeast is resolving blue as primary for a larger proportion. If blue has a bug/old config this can explain timeouts.
Mike: Customer impact - CS reporting 3 enterprise customers in APAC on degraded service. CS-Rep: collecting account list now.
Deploy Bot: Canary kill-switch available: flag `canary_blue_ap_northeast`.
Jordan: Immediate plan: 1) flip kill-switch to stop routing new canary traffic to blue in ap-northeast, 2) roll back blue instances if necessary, 3) push DNS weight correction and flush local caches. Who can flip flag?
Kei: I will flip the flag now. Executing API: POST /flags/canary_blue_ap_northeast {"value":false}
Kei: response 200 OK
SRE-Oncall: After flag flip, new requests should go to green; however existing TCP connections and CDN DNS caches mean errors may persist briefly. Watch metrics.
Ops: Initiating rollback for blue in ap-northeast to previous stable image. Command: 
```
./deploy rollback --region ap-northeast --service api --to-image stable-2026.03.10
```
Deploy Bot: Rollback job rb/1796004321-1 started - terminating 4 blue instances in ap-northeast and redeploying stable image.
SRE-Oncall: Error rate dropping from ~35% -> ~6% over 4 minutes. Latency improving.
CS-Rep: Affected customers list: Acme AP, Sakura Cloud, Kori Labs. CS has notified account teams and opened support escalations.
Jordan: DNS root cause investigation: control plane applied geo-weight updates but ap-northeast's DNS agent pulled a stale zone file; replication lag + local resolver TTL (180s) caused split-brain routing.
Mike: Evidence: DNS zone serial shows change at 1796004200, but ap-northeast agent last fetched at 1796004250 then failed to refresh until 1796004800. Logs attached to incident doc.
Ops: We've forced a zone reload and reduced TTL temporarily to 30s. Also issuing a cache purge on forwarding resolvers where possible.
SRE-Oncall: Monitoring 30 minutes. If ap-northeast errors >1% alert SRE. Handoff to Jordan for the next hour.
Jordan: Taking watch. Thanks. I'll keep dashboards up and coordinate CS for any lingering customer callbacks.
Deploy Bot: Rollback completed successfully (job id rb/1796004321-1). All ap-northeast instances running stable image.
SRE-Oncall: Final status: error rate back to baseline (~0.5%), latencies within SLO. Incident mitigated at 1796006123.
Jordan: Incident opened in PagerDuty INC-3910 (sev=P1). Post-action items: add geo-consistency check to rollout pipeline (verify DNS serials match across regions before shifting >5%), implement a pre-rollout DNS agent health check, and document kill-switch runbook including who can flip flags.
Kei: I'll open PR for the pipeline check and start a runbook draft. OPS ticket OSREQ-256 filed to add DNS cache purge step during rollouts.
Mike: CS note: three customers affected for ~12-18 minutes during peak. Legal and sales notified.
Jordan: I'll take owner of the postmortem with Ops and Deploy. We'll schedule a 30m follow-up to review timeline and logs tomorrow. Please add any logs/screenshots to the incident doc.
SRE-Oncall: Closing pager. :white_check_mark:
